paper.review_basis: Parsed original-paper transcription; original typeset pages not visually verified.

supported_facts: Printed pages 683-684: sample particle-size measurements were unavailable; regressions used representative USDA textural-class compositions from Table 2.
Table 5: regressions estimate class means and within-class standard deviations. These deviations are not confidence intervals for fitted means.
Printed page 683: retention was converted from mass to volume using density; saturation used an assumed particle density of 2.65.
pending: Migrate explicit logarithmic units and distinguish model parameters from within-class dispersions without altering regression expressions.
Register a verifiable USDA-class-to-Table-2 midpoint derivation; do not relabel derived class coordinates as measured sample texture.
Review the source power-curve support and do not invent a near-saturation branch.
Retain parameter covariation limitations and empirical uncertainty insufficiency.
decision: Pinned source-linked software resolves the prior logarithmic-base evidence gap. Manifest migration and real candidate registration remain pending; no Cosby formulas or bindings changed in this checkpoint.

source_linked_implementation.locations: Lines 83-103, explicitly named pedotransf_cosby1984_table5; outputs declare suction mm and conductivity mm/s.
supported_facts: The exact 1.88-0.0131*sand and -0.884+0.0153*sand regressions are back-transformed with base 10.
The suction factor 10 converts original cm to output mm, consistent with the original article.
The rounded conductivity factor 0.0070556 mm/s is consistent with 25.4/3600 mm/s per inch/hour; interpreting the original unit is a corroborated inference.
source_linked_implementation.limitations: This software corroborates the mean-regression logarithmic convention. It does not provide confidence coverage, resolve within-class covariance, or justify raw measured-texture use as the original class-midpoint calibration protocol.
